goal: Migrate Ledger Account Categories to the managed Effect runtime without changing HTTP, domain, error, persistence, transaction, concurrency, identifier, timestamp, tenancy, or operational behavior.

tasks.name: Migrate Category CRUD persistence
inputs: Approved persistence and error baseline in design.md
Shared NotFoundError, ConflictError, and PostgreSQL cause inspection
tasks.description: Define the Effect repository contract, tag, live implementation, and Layer. Convert list, get, upsert, and delete to native Effect Drizzle while preserving Ledger-only predicates, created-descending ordering, pagination, conflict clauses, returned rows, cascade behavior, error details, and timestamp ownership. Adapt the PostgreSQL repository harness to run repository Effects. Add no Organization predicate, transaction, retry, lock, or error hierarchy.

tests: Empty, paginated, and descending-order lists behave unchanged.
Get hides missing and cross-Ledger Categories with the existing Not Found details.
Upsert preserves insert, replacement, immutable Ledger mismatch, nullable fields, metadata, and timestamps.
Delete preserves Ledger isolation, missing-row behavior, and junction-table cascades.
acceptance: The live repository uses DatabaseTag.effectDb.
Missing Ledger foreign keys and zero-row upserts retain their existing public errors.
Unexpected SQL and row-decoding failures remain generic internal server failures.
No Organization scoping, transaction, retry, lock, or schema change is introduced.

tasks.name: Migrate Category relationship persistence
inputs: Existing Account and parent junction-table behavior
Existing sequential existence checks and PostgreSQL constraints
tasks.description: Convert the four Account and parent relationship operations to Effects. Preserve the exact sequence of existence reads and writes, duplicate-link idempotency, missing-link details, multiple parents, direct self-link rejection, and cascade behavior. Keep each statement independent and nontransactional. Do not add full cycle detection or verify that linked Accounts belong to the Category's Ledger.

tests: Duplicate Account and parent links remain successful and idempotent.
Missing Accounts, Categories, and relationships retain their current Not Found details.
Parent links continue to allow multiple parents and reject only direct self-links.
Cross-Ledger Category access remains hidden while cross-Ledger Account links retain current behavior.
acceptance: Existence checks and writes execute in their existing order.
Relationship operations add no transaction, lock, retry, cycle detection, or tenancy hardening.

tasks.name: Remove Category from legacy repository wiring
inputs: Current legacy repository plugin and shared test fixtures
tasks.description: Remove only Category construction, plugin typing, and fixture exposure from the Node Drizzle repository wiring. Keep Settlement, Statement, and Balance Monitor repository wiring unchanged.

tests: Category repository tests obtain the repository through the Effect Layer.
Remaining legacy repository tests continue to use their existing fixtures.
acceptance: No production or test code constructs the old Category repository with DrizzleDB.
Remaining legacy repositories and their injection options are unchanged.

tasks.name: Migrate Category service orchestration
inputs: Existing service method names and argument conventions
Current ID parsing and entity construction behavior
tasks.description: Convert all nine service methods to Effects and add the service tag and Layer. Preserve direct delegation for reads, deletion, and relationships. Create continues to construct one entity and upsert it. Update continues to parse IDs, perform a separate existence read, construct replacement state, and perform the existing ID-based upsert. Keep that sequence nontransactional and last-writer-wins. Replace the handwritten request mirror with the existing TypeBox-derived type and adapt tests to provide an Effect repository stub.

tests: Every method calls the same repository operation with the same arguments.
Create preserves TypeID generation and entity conversion.
Update proves the existence read completes before upsert.
A failed existence read prevents the update upsert.
Repository errors propagate unchanged through the Effect error channel.
acceptance: The service Layer composes with a repository test Layer.
PUT remains a separate read followed by ID-based upsert with no transaction, lock, retry, or idempotency key.
No handwritten mirror request type remains.

tasks.name: Compose Categories into the server runtime
tasks.description: Add the Category service to ServerRuntimeServices, provide its repository Layer, and merge it into the existing server Layer. Remove only Category types, construction, decoration, and injection from the legacy service plugin. Keep all other runtime services and legacy service wiring unchanged. Add no Category-specific runtime, override API, resource lifetime, or generic executor.

tests: The Category service resolves from the managed server runtime.
The Category service Layer composes with its repository Layer.
acceptance: The default runtime supplies DatabaseTag.effectDb to the Category repository.
Server shutdown retains the existing managed database finalizer.
Settlement, Statement, and Balance Monitor services remain available through the legacy plugin.

tasks.name: Run all Category routes through Effect
inputs: Organization, Account, and Transaction route execution patterns
Existing Category schemas, permissions, route tests, and global error handler
tasks.description: Update all nine handlers to obtain the Category service from its tag, execute one Effect through request.server.runtime, and rethrow failures to the existing global error handler. Preserve paths, methods, operation IDs, permissions, request parsing, response conversion, advertised schemas, success codes, headers, pagination defaults, and empty mutation responses. Adapt route tests to install a complete Category service with Layer.succeed and return successful or failed Effects.

tests: All nine handlers execute through the supplied runtime.
List and get return the same response representations.
Create and PUT remain 200 and create emits no Location header.
Delete, link, and unlink remain 200 with empty responses.
Validation, authentication, permissions, Not Found, Conflict, and generic internal server behavior remain unchanged.
acceptance: Route paths, methods, schemas, permissions, operation IDs, statuses, and headers are unchanged.
Existing 429 and 503 schemas remain advertised without new Category producers.
Routes use the existing server runtime and global error handler without a new adapter.

tasks.name: Validate the migration and audit deviations
inputs: Baseline result of 32 API test files and 490 tests
tasks.description: Run focused tests followed by the full API and repository checks. Compare the final diff with the recorded baseline. Stop and split out any HTTP, domain, error, SQL, transaction, concurrency, identifier, timestamp, tenancy, or operational deviation.

tests: pnpm --filter=@exchequerio/api test -- src/repo/LedgerAccountCategoryRepo.test.ts
pnpm --filter=@exchequerio/api test -- src/services/LedgerAccountCategoryService.test.ts
pnpm --filter=@exchequerio/api test -- src/routes/ledgers/LedgerAccountCategoryRoutes.test.ts
pnpm --filter=@exchequerio/api test
pnpm --filter=@exchequerio/api types
pnpm --filter=@exchequerio/api build
pnpm run check
pnpm run ci
acceptance: git diff --check passes.
The diff contains no entity, TypeBox schema, database schema, migration, dependency, or unrelated cleanup changes.
Organization scoping, OCC, lock_version, transactions, retries, idempotency keys, real balances, cycle detection, and relationship hardening are absent.
Any discovered deviation is moved to a separately approved plan and change set before implementation continues.
